For x>sqrt(2at/h), sign F’ equals sign(w-W(x)); W’ has sign Q(x)=Delta*x^3+6at*x^2+6at^2*x+2a^2*t^3, Delta=2a-(1-a)ht. Delta>=0 implies increasing W approaching w_infty from below, yielding one finite optimum for w<w_infty and strictly increasing F otherwise. Delta<0 gives exactly one positive cubic root q by Descartes, hence one spinodal ws=W(q); the plateau comparison F_w(x)-tw is a positive factor times H(x)-w, and H’ has a unique positive zero z, giving wc=H(z), w_infty<wc<ws and metastability. The large-x W expansion proves exponent 1 for Delta>0 and 1/2 at Delta=0. Independent symbolic algebra verified all five rational identities and derivative factorizations, not merely printed CHECK.py output.
